name: Methenolone

lead: Methenolone (Primobolan) is an anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone, available as an oral acetate and an injectable enanthate. In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums it is regarded as a mild compound for lean gains with fewer estrogenic effects, for a leaner, harder physique.

It binds the androgen receptor and promotes protein synthesis, and the enanthate is a long-acting injectable. Controlled studies are medical: a 1979 trial in refractory anemias, 1975 and later work in breast cancer, and a 2011 randomized trial in 26 stroke patients in which weekly injections increased thigh muscle area compared with controls. No study has tested it for physique in healthy people.

paras: Users add it to lean-gain or cutting phases, often with other compounds, and describe slow, steady changes over a long run. The oral acetate is limited by first-pass liver metabolism, while the enanthate is a long-acting injectable.

Trials in refractory anemia reported negligible side effects, but one trial found more marked anemia and thrombocytopenia in lymphoma patients given methenolone during chemotherapy, and a rat study found worse cirrhosis-like liver changes with the acetate. Forum users report liver problems and dispute how harsh it is on lipids. It is prohibited in sport.

chain: Lean muscle gained with less water
angle.text: Methenolone (Primobolan) is a mild DHT-derived steroid that users favour for lean muscle gain with fewer side effects, building a leaner, harder physique. A 2011 randomized trial in stroke patients found thigh-muscle gains; trials in healthy people for physique are absent.

lead: Methenolone (also metenolone; brand name Primobolan) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone, available as an oral acetate and an injectable enanthate ester. Wikipedia reports that it was introduced for medical use in the early 1960s, mainly for anemia caused by bone marrow failure, and that it has also been used for wasting, osteoporosis, sarcopenia and weight gain in underweight infants and children.[1]

Its appearance connection is muscle: in bodybuilding circles, methenolone is regarded as a lean-gain compound, with athletes said to favour it for dry, defined looks during cutting phases because it is thought to add muscle with little water retention, according to Grokipedia, which is AI-generated.[2] The compound is a mild-looking entry on forum lists of steroids, and it does not convert to estrogen, which is why users associate it with a hard, dry look.[1][2]

Human studies are clinical. A 19-patient trial of Primobolan in refractory anemias reported remissions in some subtypes with negligible side effects; a 1975 study of the enanthate in disseminated breast cancer reported objective remission in 8 of 41 evaluable patients and described the agent as less virilising than testosterone propionate; and a 2011 randomized trial in 26 hemiplegic stroke patients found larger thigh-muscle gains on weekly injections than in controls.[3][4] No controlled study has measured its effects on appearance in healthy users.
It is a controlled substance in many countries, including Schedule III in the United States, and is prohibited in sport by the World Anti-Doping Agency.[1]

paras: Methenolone is also known as 1-methyl-DHT or 1-methyl-5-alpha-androst-1-en-17-beta-ol-3-one, with the formula C20H30O2 and a molar mass of about 302 g/mol. The acetate and enanthate esters are prodrugs of the parent compound. Wikipedia notes it should not be confused with metandienone, a different steroid.[1]

Grokipedia says Schering AG developed it in the early 1960s by adding a methyl group at carbon 1 and a double bond between carbons 1 and 2 of dihydrotestosterone, and that it was sold as Primobolan in Europe and Nibal Depot in the United States.[2]

A 1979 trial treated 19 consecutive patients with refractory anemias using methenolone; remission frequencies were 3 of 6 in pancytopenia, 2 of 4 in bicytopenia, 1 of 5 in refractory anemia with hyperplastic marrow and 1 of 4 in myelofibrosis, with no obvious prolongation of survival among responders and negligible side effects.[3] A case report described a patient with thymoma-associated pure red cell aplasia treated with cyclosporine and Primobolan who remained transfusion-dependent.

In 1975 investigators treated 43 patients with disseminated breast carcinoma using metenolone enanthate at weekly doses; objective remissions longer than three months occurred in 8 of 41 evaluable patients, soft-tissue metastases responded best, and the authors judged its efficacy comparable to testosterone propionate but less virilising. In 1977 a randomized trial in lymphoma found that adding high-dose metenolone during MOPP chemotherapy increased rather than reduced hematological toxicity.[5]

A 1968 randomized trial examined methenolone enanthate in advanced breast cancer, and a Japanese case report described an aplastic anemia patient who had been treated with granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, erythropoietin and methenolone acetate.[6][7] Grokipedia says medical use peaked in the 1970s and 1980s and declined after erythropoietin became available.[2]

In forums, users describe methenolone as a lean-gain compound used on its own in TRT contexts or alongside testosterone and nandrolone.[8][9] A T Nation poster said his wife gained roughly ten pounds of muscle in four weeks on metenolone but stopped after liver issues, an anecdote with no controlled data.[10] Others say compounds that make users look big, such as nandrolone or methandienone, are no better at building muscle than Winstrol, Primobolan or Masteron.[11]

Clinical studies include a 19-patient trial in refractory anemias, a 1975 breast-cancer study of the enanthate, a 1977 randomized trial in lymphoma during chemotherapy and a 2011 randomized trial of 26 stroke patients showing larger thigh-muscle gains on weekly injections.[3][5][4] There are no trials in healthy people for appearance.

In a randomized trial of 26 subacute stroke patients, weekly injections of metenolone enanthate for six weeks increased thigh cross-sectional area on CT by 13.4 percent on the affected side and 14.5 percent on the unaffected side, versus 3.3 and 5.2 percent in controls, without specific training; the authors concluded it was effective for improving muscle area in stroke rehabilitation.[4] A related study examined anabolic steroid administration combined with passive muscle stretching on expression of a muscle growth factor. No trial has tested methenolone for bodybuilding or appearance in healthy people.

The refractory-anemia trial reported negligible side effects, whereas the lymphoma trial reported more marked anemia and thrombocytopenia with methenolone plus chemotherapy.[3][5] In rats with thioacetamide-induced cirrhosis, methenolone acetate treatment was followed by more serious structural liver alterations than in untreated animals. A rat study cited on T Nation examined cardiac effects of metenolone enanthate during puberty.[12][9]

Forum posters differ on its safety: one says it is safer than testosterone at high doses though harsher on lipids, another argues it may be less toxic acutely than testosterone at supraphysiologic doses, and a patient on T Nation says he added it to a TRT protocol for ulcerative colitis.[13][14][15]

Methenolone is an androgen receptor agonist with moderate anabolic and weak androgenic effects. Wikipedia reports no estrogenic effects, because it does not aromatize, and says its double bond at carbons 1 and 2 makes it resistant to the enzyme 3-alpha-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, which gives it more anabolic activity than DHT, mestanolone or mesterolone. In rodents, its androgenic-to-anabolic ratio is about 1:2 to 1:3, and its affinity for sex hormone-binding globulin is about 16 percent that of testosterone and 3 percent that of DHT.[1] Grokipedia gives a higher rodent ratio and states that it binds extensively to plasma proteins and is metabolised in the liver by CYP3A4.[2]

The acetate is taken by mouth and is limited by first-pass liver metabolism, with a half-life of hours, whereas the enanthate is injected and released over roughly one to two weeks, according to Grokipedia.[2] Anti-doping chemists have characterised its urinary metabolites, including long-term sulfate metabolites that extend the detection window, and a 1990 study identified new urinary metabolites of methenolone acetate in humans.[16][17]

A 1975 study of six anabolic steroids in men with ischaemic heart disease found that five 17-alpha-alkylated steroids enhanced plasma fibrinolytic activity, whereas methenolone acetate, the only non-17-alpha-alkylated steroid tested, did not.[18] A 1994 review of hormonal therapy in nutrition describes nandrolone, stanolone and methenolone as associated with protein anabolism and minimal androgenizing action.[19] A 2026 review notes that cryo-EM structures of methenolone bound to an adhesion receptor have been reported, part of basic research on steroid binding outside classic androgen receptors, which a 2025 Cell paper also addresses.[20][21]

In bodybuilding, a 1989 survey of competitive bodybuilders in Kansas and Missouri found that 54 percent of male competitors used steroids regularly compared with 10 percent of female competitors, and a Flemish analysis of unannounced doping controls from 1988 to 1993 found that in some federations 38 to 58 percent of tested bodybuilders were positive.[22][23] These studies describe steroid use generally, not methenolone alone.

On T Nation, methenolone is mentioned among compounds added to TRT regimens for wellness and in lean-bulk stack discussions.[8][9] Wikipedia lists known doping cases among professional athletes and says the compound is banned by WADA and by the NBA and NBPA; Grokipedia adds that illicit demand sustains a black market in which products may be counterfeit or impure.[1][2]

Wikipedia lists methenolone as Class C5 in Brazil, Schedule IV in Canada and Schedule III in the United States, and says non-medical use is generally illicit where it is controlled.[1] Grokipedia states it is a prescription-only medicine in the EU and Class C in the UK, that no FDA-approved products exist in the US, and that it was withdrawn from the US market in the early 1990s.[2]

A 2024 randomized trial in rats evaluated methenolone enanthate for preventing medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw, and a registered study (NCT07568574) plans to examine medically supervised performance-enhancing substances in elite athletes.[24][25] A 2004 rat study of nandrolone, metenolone acetate and dromostanolone examined endocrine and pathological changes.[26]

lore.intro: Primobolan is discussed on T Nation as a mild compound for lean gains, with claims about lower toxicity and disagreement over its effect on lipids.[13][14][11]

claims.claim: Primobolan is a milder, safer steroid.
Primobolan does not aromatize, so it gives a dry look without estrogenic water retention.
Fake or underdosed Primobolan is common on the black market.

timeline.event: Methenolone is introduced as Primobolan and Nibal Depot, according to Grokipedia; Wikipedia gives the early 1960s.[2][1]
A randomized trial examines methenolone enanthate in advanced breast cancer.[6]
Treatment of disseminated breast carcinoma with metenolone enanthate is reported.
A randomized trial finds more hematological toxicity with metenolone during lymphoma chemotherapy.[5]
A trial of methenolone in refractory anemias is published.[3]
A survey of competitive bodybuilders documents regular steroid use.[22]
Urinary metabolites of methenolone acetate are characterised, supporting detection in doping control.[17]
A randomized trial reports thigh-muscle gains in stroke patients given metenolone enanthate.[4]
A Cell paper reports the identification, structure and agonist design of an androgen membrane receptor; a 2026 review notes cryo-EM structures of methenolone bound to an adhesion receptor.[21][20]
